go-fundamentals-sr1-11.reason: source_problem: the spec only permits the restriction. The FAQ states that Go refuses to compile unused variables. The explanation now names both, and the statement and answer are unchanged. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr1-11.statement: The gc compiler rejects an unused local variable introduced by a var declaration.
go-fundamentals-sr1-11.explanation: The spec lets a compiler reject a local variable that is never used, and the gc toolchain does: the Go FAQ says Go refuses to compile programs with unused variables.

source.title: Go FAQ: Can I stop these complaints about my unused variable/import?

go-fundamentals-sr2-09.reason: source_problem: strings.Compare does not say the comparison is byte-wise. The spec's Comparison operators section says "Two string values are compared lexically byte-wise." The explanation is tidied, and the statement and answer are unchanged. (final: fixed)
go-fundamentals-sr2-09.statement: The comparison `"Z" < "a"` uses case-insensitive alphabetic ordering.
go-fundamentals-sr2-09.explanation: The spec compares two strings lexically byte-wise and does no case folding. 'Z' is byte 0x5A and 'a' is 0x61, so "Z" < "a" is true: every upper-case ASCII letter sorts before every lower-case one.
go-fundamentals-sr2-09.misconception: String comparison folds letter case before ordering.

go-fundamentals-sr4-05.reason: weak_card (comma-ok definition card). Rewritten instead of dropped because r4 lost four true cards; dropping all of them would leave 8 cards at 2T/6F. The new card tests presence versus a stored zero value. Spec Index expressions: "The value of ok is true if the key x is present in the map, and false otherwise." Suggested factKey: map-lookup-present-zero-value. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr4-05.statement: For a key k stored with value 0, `v, ok := m[k]` sets ok to true.
go-fundamentals-sr4-05.explanation: ok reports whether key k is present in the map, whatever its element holds, so a key stored with 0 gives v == 0 and ok == true. An absent key gives false.

go-fundamentals-sr4-07.reason: duplicate of sr3-11 (one clear distinction, slice versus map) and a name giveaway. Rewritten for r4 balance with the verifier's map element addressability card, an uncovered r4 fact. Spec Assignment statements: "Each left-hand side operand must be addressable, a map index expression, or (for = assignments only) the blank identifier." Address operators does not list map indexing as addressable. Suggested factKey: map-element-not-addressable. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr4-07.statement: With `m := map[string]struct{ X int }{}`, the assignment `m["a"].X = 1` fails to compile.
go-fundamentals-sr4-07.explanation: Map elements are not addressable, so a field of a struct element cannot be assigned in place. Store a whole new element with m["a"] = v, or use a map of pointers.

go-fundamentals-sr6-07.reason: source_problem plus explanation_error: Assignability states only the premise, and the old explanation credited the check to the blank identifier. Effective Go #blank_implements (Interface checks) states the idiom: "the assignment involving a conversion of a *RawMessage to a Marshaler requires that *RawMessage implements Marshaler, and that property will be checked at compile time." (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr6-07.statement: For a method interface `I`, `var _ I = (*T)(nil)` checks `*T`'s implementation at compile time.
go-fundamentals-sr6-07.explanation: Assigning (*T)(nil) to I requires *T to implement I, so the declaration fails to compile if a method is missing; the blank identifier just discards the value.

go-fundamentals-sr8-11.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation never stated when deferred calls do run. The new one states the right fact from the spec's Defer statements section. It leaves out "or panics" so that it does not give away sr10-10. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr8-11.statement: A `defer` inside a loop runs its scheduled call when that loop iteration ends.
go-fundamentals-sr8-11.explanation: Deferred calls run when the surrounding function returns, not when a loop iteration ends, so a defer in a loop body keeps each iteration's call pending until the function exits.
go-fundamentals-sr8-11.misconception: A loop iteration defines the execution boundary for calls deferred inside it.

go-fundamentals-sr13-01.reason: source_problem: the 2022 intro-generics post does not state the default-type rule. Spec Type inference: an untyped constant for a bound type parameter is "collected separately", and "The type argument for Pk is the default type for the determined constant kind." The explanation now names that mechanism. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr13-01.statement: Given `func id[T any](x T) T`, a call written as `id(7)` instantiates id with the type argument int.
go-fundamentals-sr13-01.explanation: 7 is an untyped constant, so inference uses its default type: with no typed argument for T, the spec infers int, the default type of an integer constant.

source.title: The Go Programming Language Specification: Type inference

go-fundamentals-sr14-02.reason: ambiguous: "package-level identifier" also covers an imported package name, which has file-block scope. The statement now says "variable". The source moves from the unanchored FAQ root to the spec's Declarations and scope, which says top-level variables have package-block scope and imported package names have file-block scope. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr14-02.statement: A package-level variable named cache has scope limited to the source file that declares it.
go-fundamentals-sr14-02.explanation: A variable declared at top level has package-block scope, so every file of the same package can use cache, whatever its case. Imported package names, by contrast, are scoped to the file that imports them.
go-fundamentals-sr14-02.misconception: A lower-case package-level variable is visible only in the file that declares it.

source.title: The Go Programming Language Specification: Declarations and scope

go-fundamentals-sr7-12.reason: tell: "The compiler accepts ..." was false in 4 of 4 cards. Reworded with the same fact and answer. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr7-12.statement: A struct type T with a function-valued field M can also have a method M declared on T.
go-fundamentals-sr7-12.explanation: A struct's non-blank, directly declared field names and bound method names must be distinct. A function-valued field receives no exception.
go-fundamentals-sr7-12.misconception: A function-valued field permits a same-named method on its struct type.

go-fundamentals-sr8-01.reason: tell: "The compiler accepts ..." was false in 4 of 4 cards. Reworded with the same fact and answer; "valid" was skewed toward true, so this also balances it. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr8-01.statement: `f == g` is valid for two variables f and g that share the same function type.
go-fundamentals-sr8-01.explanation: Go permits a function value to be compared with nil. Comparing two function values with == is a compile-time error.
go-fundamentals-sr8-01.misconception: Function values with matching types support equality comparisons.

go-fundamentals-sr13-06.reason: tell: "The compiler accepts ..." was false in 4 of 4 cards. Reworded with the same fact and answer, and with the length kept close to the original. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr13-06.statement: `interface{ int | int }` is a legal type constraint for the type parameter of a generic function.
go-fundamentals-sr13-06.explanation: Non-interface union terms need disjoint type sets. Repeating int makes this constraint illegal.
go-fundamentals-sr13-06.misconception: Union constraints accept repeated non-interface terms.

go-fundamentals-sr14-04.reason: tell: "The compiler accepts ..." was false in 4 of 4 cards. Reworded with the same fact and answer; using the hedge verb "lets" on a false card balances hedge verbs. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr14-04.statement: Go lets package a import package b when package b already imports package a.
go-fundamentals-sr14-04.explanation: Go rejects a package importing itself through another package; the resulting import cycle is illegal.
go-fundamentals-sr14-04.misconception: Packages can import one another in a cycle.

go-fundamentals-sr5-03.reason: tell: a statement opening with "If" was true in 6 of 6 cards. Reworded with the same fact and answer. (final: keep)
go-fundamentals-sr5-03.statement: For a pointer `p` to a struct with field `Name`, `p.Name` accesses the same field as `(*p).Name`.
go-fundamentals-sr5-03.explanation: Go follows a struct pointer for a field selector, so p.Name abbreviates (*p).Name.
